findings.title: Effectful nodes with dead inputs not converted to Unreachable in SimplifiedLowering
findings.message: In RepresentationSelector::VisitNode, when an effectful node (one with control/effect inputs) has a value input of type None (unreachable), the introducing commit changed the handling from properly disconnecting and replacing the node with a DeadValue to simply setting is_dead=true and returning after calling InsertUnreachableIfNecessary. InsertUnreachableIfNecessary only handles the effect chain by inserting an Unreachable node after the original node; it does not convert the original effectful node itself to a DeadValue. This leaves the effectful node in the graph as its original opcode but with feedback_type set to Type::None(). The LOWER phase returns without lowering the node, and when downstream code or the verifier later calls NodeProperties::GetType() on this untyped node, the DCHECK(IsTyped(node)) assertion fails. In release builds this inconsistency could lead to miscompilation of JIT-compiled JavaScript code.
findings.suggestion: For effectful nodes with control inputs (ControlInputCount() > 0) that have None-typed value inputs, create an Unreachable node using the node's effect and control inputs, redirect all effect/control uses of the original node to the new Unreachable, and convert the original node into a DeadValue. Do not rely on InsertUnreachableIfNecessary for this case as it does not convert the node itself. The condition guarding the dead-input detection also needs to be expanded to cover nodes with ControlInputCount() > 0 (effectful nodes without control outputs).

ground_truth.root_cause: The introducing commit (9a6e625, fixing bug 424205788) refactored the dead-value handling for effectful nodes in the LOWER phase. The old approach called DisconnectFromEffectAndControl(node) followed by conversion to DeadValue. The new approach set is_dead=true, set feedback_type to None, called InsertUnreachableIfNecessary (which only patches the effect chain but doesn't replace the node itself), then returned early. This is incorrect for effectful nodes with control inputs: the node remains in the graph as its original operation but with a None type, violating the invariant that all nodes in the lowered graph must be either properly typed or replaced by appropriate dead-code nodes.
